name: WooCommerce
title: WooCommerce SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on WooCommerce: 27 of 43 services wired. Cart and checkout work through the Store API; sign-in cannot, as core has no endpoint for it.
lede: WooCommerce is three APIs with three auth models: `wc/v3` with a consumer key and secret, the Store API `wc/store/v1` with a session Cart-Token — where the cart and checkout live — and WordPress core’s `wp/v2`. The connector uses all three.
verdict: Cart and checkout are wired through WooCommerce’s Store API, so shoppers can check out; they cannot sign in, because WooCommerce core has no endpoint that returns a shopper session. Read the note on the consumer key before deploying: the connector takes it from a `PUBLIC_` variable, which the browser receives.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your WordPress site

env.name: PUBLIC_WOOCOMMERCE_API_URL
env.note: Your WordPress site’s URL. The connector adds `/wp-json/wc/v3`, `/wp-json/wc/store/v1` and `/wp-json/wp/v2`. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_WOOCOMMERCE_API_KEY
env.note: A WooCommerce REST API consumer key, sent as HTTP Basic to `wc/v3` — products, orders, coupons and customers. See the limitations.

env.name: PUBLIC_WOOCOMMERCE_API_SECRET
env.note: The consumer secret that goes with it.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/woocommerce-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_WOOCOMMERCE_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_WOOCOMMERCE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `PUBLIC_WOOCOMMERCE_ACCESS_KEY`, `PUBLIC_WOOCOMMERCE_STORE_ID` and `PUBLIC_WOOCOMMERCE_CHANNEL_ID`; the connector’s source does not read them. The guide’s own example sets only the URL — the key and secret here are what `wc/v3` calls authenticate with.
backendSettings: Create a REST API key under WooCommerce › Settings › Advanced › REST API for `PUBLIC_WOOCOMMERCE_API_KEY` and `PUBLIC_WOOCOMMERCE_API_SECRET` — and read the limitations first.
Keep pretty permalinks on: the connector calls `/wp-json/…` paths.
Let the storefront’s origin make cross-origin requests to WordPress (CORS): in production the browser calls `PUBLIC_WOOCOMMERCE_API_URL` directly, not only the server.
howItWorks: The connector reads the catalogue, orders, coupons and customers from `wc/v3` with the consumer key and secret; runs the cart and checkout through the Store API, `wc/store/v1`, where a session Cart-Token carries the basket; and reads pages from WordPress core’s `wp/v2`. Cart and checkout exist only in the Store API.
limitations: The consumer key and secret the connector sends to `wc/v3` come from `PUBLIC_WOOCOMMERCE_API_KEY` and `PUBLIC_WOOCOMMERCE_API_SECRET`. SvelteKit sends `PUBLIC_` variables to the browser, so every visitor to the store can read them and call `wc/v3` with whatever permissions the key has.

faq.q: Can I run a WooCommerce store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Shoppers can browse, fill a cart and check out through WooCommerce’s Store API; they cannot sign in, and there is no wishlist. Before deploying, weigh the consumer key: the connector reads it from a `PUBLIC_` variable, which every visitor’s browser receives.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to WooCommerce?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/woocommerce-connector`, set `PUBLIC_WOOCOMMERCE_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: Why can’t shoppers sign in on WooCommerce?
faq.a: WooCommerce core has no endpoint that returns a shopper session: `POST /customers` creates an account but hands back no session. Rather than fake one, the connector’s `auth` throws. The Svelte Commerce maintainers have asked WooCommerce’s maintainers whether a supported path exists without a JWT plugin.

openQuestion: Is there any supported path to customer login without a JWT plugin? Today `auth` throws, because `POST /customers` creates an account but returns no session.

api.surface: The connector calls three WordPress REST namespaces on the store’s own URL: WooCommerce `wc/v3` at `/wp-json/wc/v3` for the catalogue, orders and customers, the Store API at `/wp-json/wc/store/v1` for the cart and checkout, and WordPress core at `/wp-json/wp/v2` for pages.
api.auth: Calls to `wc/v3` carry the consumer key and secret as `Authorization: Basic`; Store API calls carry no key and instead replay the `Cart-Token` and `Nonce` headers captured from the previous response, with the cart token also kept in `localStorage` as `cart_id`; shopper sign-in is not possible, because every sign-in method throws `NotSupportedError`.

calls.what: `GET /wp-json/wc/v3/products` with `page`, `per_page`, `search`, `orderby`, `order` and `status=publish`; a product page by slug uses `GET /products?slug=`, then `GET /products/{id}/variations?per_page=100`
`GET /wp-json/wc/v3/products/categories`, by `slug` or numeric id, and `GET /products?category={id}` for a category’s products
`GET /wp-json/wc/v3/products` with `search`, `category`, `tag`, `min_price` and `max_price`, plus `GET /wp-json/wc/store/v1/products/collection-data?calculate_price_range=true` for the price range

`GET /wp-json/wc/v3/payment_gateways` (or `/payment_gateways/cod`) to find an enabled gateway, then `POST /wp-json/wc/store/v1/checkout` with `billing_address`, `shipping_address`, `payment_method` and `payment_data`
`GET` and `PUT /wp-json/wc/v3/customers/{id}`, reading and writing the customer’s `billing` and `shipping` blocks

rules: List totals come from the `X-WP-Total` and `X-WP-TotalPages` response headers, not the body, and a route that sends neither falls back to the length of the returned array.

Sorting goes out as an `orderby` and `order` pair, `orderby` is limited to the values WooCommerce accepts (`date`, `modified`, `id`, `title`, `slug`, `price`, `popularity`, `rating`, `menu_order`), and an unknown sort becomes `date` `desc` rather than a `rest_invalid_param` error.

`GET /products/{id}` takes only a numeric id, so a product page reached by slug first runs `GET /products?slug=&per_page=1`, then fetches variations 100 at a time, which is WooCommerce’s maximum page size.
Every Store API write needs the `Nonce` from an earlier response as well as the `Cart-Token`, so the connector captures both from the response headers on every cart call.

WooCommerce has no endpoint that confirms a payment, so the connector leaves every capture method unimplemented rather than marking an order paid with `set_paid`, and only `cod`, WooCommerce’s own gateway, is driven end to end.
